claims.text: The starting monolithic CoCrFeNi alloy has a uniform microstructure.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits relatively high coefficients of friction across a broad sliding-temperature range.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits relatively high wear rates across a broad sliding-temperature range.
Adding 1–3 wt% Y2O3 through an optimized melting and casting process can produce finely and uniformly dispersed Y2O3 particles in CoCrFeNi.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles act as nucleation centers for oxide-scale formation at the sliding interface.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles promote and stabilize a lubricious oxide scale during sliding.
Y2O3 facilitates controlled oxidation of the contacting surfaces during sliding.
Y2O3-assisted oxidation produces a continuous and adherent lubricious oxide film.
The lubricious oxide film is self-replenishing during sliding.
The lubricious oxide film reduces interfacial shear stress and thereby lowers the coefficient of friction.
The lubricious oxide film protects the alloy from degradation and thereby reduces wear.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, CoCrFeNi containing 1–3 wt% Y2O3 will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, CoCrFeNi containing 1–3 wt% Y2O3 will have a consistently lower wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
The friction and wear improvements will be especially significant at high temperatures up to 800 °C.
The predicted tribological improvement applies in ambient air under moderate-to-high mechanical loads.
